system_description.narrative_title: Tectonic Flux: War, Energy, Markets and China–West Competition
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is shifting under the combined pressure of regional wars (Middle East and Ukraine), a reordering of energy flows, and rising financial-market stress as bond yields surge. Major-power competition — especially China–EU industrial rivalry and US–Russia energy diplomacy — is interacting with sanctions, supply-chain reconfiguration and AI/tech-driven economic shifts to produce cascading economic and security effects. States and markets are responding with ad hoc measures (currency defence, import caps, military posturing) that add volatility and feedbacks across the system.
system_description.scope: Interconnected global political, economic, security and technological processes driving state and market behaviour: major powers (US, China, Russia, EU), regional conflicts (Middle East, Ukraine), energy markets and shipping, global financial and bond markets, trade and industrial policy (autos, EVs), sanctions, and tech/AI diffusion and risks.
system_description.super_system: The broader globalised international system — the integrated 21st-century political-economic-environmental order in which states, markets and societies interact.
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East energy-security subsystem (Gulf conflicts, shipping, oil & gas flows)
Global financial‑monetary subsystem (sovereign bond markets, central banks, FX)
China‑centred industrial & trade subsystem (autos, EVs, supply chains, tech policy)

variables.name: Gulf proxy and maritime campaign
variables.description: Iran and Iran-aligned militias versus Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states are mounting sustained missile, drone and air/sea strikes that are escalating cross‑border violence and degrading regional connectivity.

variables.name: Russia‑Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, supported by Western allies, remain locked in a protracted high‑intensity war that is reshaping NATO deterrence, alliance cohesion and battlefield dynamics.

variables.name: China‑West industrial and tech rivalry
variables.description: China and Western powers (EU, US) are contesting industrial and technology leadership—notably autos, EVs, semiconductors and payments—via tariffs, export curbs and investment controls that are reordering supply chains and market access.

variables.name: Global energy market volatility
variables.description: Global energy markets are being driven by shifting producer export policies, OPEC demand revisions and disruptions to refining and shipping capacity, producing acute price and supply swings that reconfigure trade flows.

variables.name: Global bond‑market and monetary stress
variables.description: Major economies' bond markets, currencies and central banks (notably US, EU and major emerging markets) are experiencing surge‑rate and policy pressures that are forcing aggressive monetary responses and raising systemic financial‑stability risks.
